claims.statement: Choosing what to compare is woefully underpowered for someone with many worktrees and PRs.
Select by PR: picking a PR shows that PR's diff.
Use the gh CLI to gather rich PR context for a rich picker.
Within a PR, a commit-level viewer comparing each commit to its predecessor to see the PR's development.
Compare felt much slower than expected on first run; a repeat was fast (likely cache).
Compare treemap is very good; dependency compare is okay and needs a real-PR evaluation.
The prior visual-git exploration project is a reference for picker and timeline patterns.
Picker must degrade gracefully without gh or network; deterministic results and no working-tree mutation continue to hold.
Commit stepping multiplies cold-scan cost unless per-file results are reused across commits.
A picked worktree compares against its open PR base when gh finds one, else merge-base with the default branch.
PRs are stacked, so the compare base must be merge-base with the PR baseRefName, not the default branch; worktree lists are large and include prunable entries; gh latency ~2s requires async loading.

shape.appetite: Medium: one sources endpoint, a picker component, worktree-as-head, and a commit stepper; compare engine and views unchanged.
shape.problem: Choosing a comparison needs typed refs; no PR, worktree, or commit-stepping support; cold compares feel slow without visibility into why.

recommended_shape.endpoint: GET /api/compare/sources -> {prs (gh pr list --json number,title,headRefName,baseRefName,headRefOid,isDraft,reviewDecision,updatedAt,statusCheckRollup,author), worktrees (git worktree list --porcelain, non-prunable, sorted by HEAD date), branches (for-each-ref heads+remotes with upstream:track)}

pick_rules.pr: base=merge-base(origin/baseRefName, headRefOid); head=headRefOid; fetch head objects if missing
pick_rules.worktree: head=scan of worktree path; base=open PR base for its branch else merge-base(default, HEAD)

recommended_shape.stepper: git rev-list --first-parent --reverse base..head; step i = c[i-1]..c[i]

success_moves: Single server seam for gh with timeout, short cache, and recorded-JSON fake in tests; picker never blocks on GitHub
Use PR baseRefName for merge-base so stacked PRs match GitHub
Sections load independently so git lists render instantly and PRs fill in
Worktree head reuses the WORKTREE path-scan and mtime cache instead of a checkout
Add per-phase timings to compare progress before optimizing parallel sides or prewarming
Stepper reuses the previous side from SideCache so each step costs at most one scan

first_proof.question: Does a gh+git sources endpoint with PR-based base resolution produce GitHub-equal diffs, including stacked PRs, with a fast picker?
first_proof.artifact: sources endpoint + picker (PR picking only) on modeler #1925 and stacked #1922
first_proof.observation: changed-file count equals gh pr view N --json changedFiles; git sections <300ms; cold-side phase timings visible
first_proof.decision_rule: match -> worktree heads and stepper; stacked mismatch -> fix base resolution (remote base ref, fetch) first

rabbit_holes: PR head commits missing locally (fork PRs, unfetched)
WORKTREE semantics generalized to another path vs SideCache keys
stepping cost on large repos without per-file reuse
